slides.title: Charting the Growth of Social-Physical HRI (spHRI): A Systematic Review Pipeline Augmented by Small Language Models
slides.highlight: This research evaluates using small language models to accelerate the screening of social-physical human-robot interaction literature, supporting the development of embodied social robots in RwB.

card.one_liner: Small language models can augment systematic reviews by recovering relevant papers missed by human screeners.
card.key_idea: A pipeline using a unanimity ensemble of four locally deployed SLMs (≤1.5B parameters) as a second-pass filter for title and abstract screening in spHRI research.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 32,000 records; SLM ensemble identified 39 missed papers (10.29% of final set), screening orders of magnitude faster than humans.
card.limitation: SLMs cannot replace expert judgment due to a precision-recall tradeoff and lack of confidence scoring in binary outputs.

slides.title: When Robots Rate Their Own Interactions: Engagement Validity and the Strangeness Failure
slides.highlight: This research explores inverted evaluation where LLM-powered robots rate their own interactions, providing insights into the boundary conditions for using AI as interaction evaluators for RwB.

card.one_liner: LLM-powered robots can accurately rate interaction engagement but systematically fail to detect human strangeness/discomfort.
card.key_idea: An 'inverted evaluation' framework where LLMs complete standardized HRI questionnaires from the robot's perspective using interaction transcripts and multimodal context.
card.evaluation: Tested via HRI-CUES dataset (5 LLMs, 1,522 evaluations) and a Nao robot pilot (N=4). Results show moderate-to-strong engagement agreement but significant strangeness inversion.
card.limitation: LLMs lack access to internal affective states, relying on behavioral proxies that conflate philosophical curiosity with comfort.

slides.title: Onconetix Announces Realbotix Optio and M-Series Humanoid Robot Pilot at Salamanca City Central School District
slides.tldr: HUMANOID ROBOT PILOT IN SCHOOL DISTRICT
slides.highlight: The pilot of Realbotix Optio and M-Series humanoid robots in a school district provides insights into embodied social robots and human-robot interaction relevant to RwB.

slides.title: EmotionAI: A Privacy-Preserving Computational Intelligence Pipeline for Speech-Emotion-Grounded Conversational Analysis
slides.highlight: This work presents a local pipeline integrating speaker diarization and emotion classification for grounded conversational analysis, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and diarization.

card.one_liner: A fully local pipeline integrating speech emotion recognition with LLMs for privacy-preserving conversational analysis.
card.key_idea: Combines pyannote diarization, Whisper ASR, and wav2vec2 SER with an adversarial three-model local LLM panel to provide timestamp-grounded, citation-constrained affective reasoning.
card.evaluation: Tested on RAVDESS (48.8% SER accuracy) and a small Q&A rubric study. CPU runtime averaged 157s for a 2-minute interview.
card.limitation: Significant cross-corpus fragility (especially for 'Sad' emotion) and lack of validation for spontaneous field audio or diverse demographics.

slides.title: GROVE: Grounded Pedestrian Simulation via Natural Language for Interactive Social Robot Navigation
slides.highlight: GROVE provides a text-to-scenario framework for generating realistic, socially challenging pedestrian simulations to improve social robot navigation. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: GROVE is a text-to-scenario framework that generates realistic, grounded pedestrian simulations for social robot navigation training.
card.key_idea: Combines LLM-based RAG for behavior tree generation, Theta* for global planning, and Social Force Models for local interaction across three behavioral horizons.
card.evaluation: Compared qualitatively and quantitatively (via GPT-5 VLM scoring) against Text-Crowd and TRACE across residential, hospital, and office environments.
card.limitation: High computational cost for inference and a reliance on static obstacle maps, ignoring dynamic environmental changes.

slides.title: Do more heads imply better performance? An empirical study of team thought leaders' impact on scientific team performance
slides.tldr: IMPACT OF THOUGHT LEADERSHIP ON TEAM PERFORMANCE
slides.highlight: This study examines how the number of thought leaders affects team impact and disruptiveness, providing insights into group dynamics relevant to HyECHO's focus on hybrid team state and engagement.

card.one_liner: More thought leaders in scientific teams have an inverted U-shaped impact on performance and reduce disruptiveness.
card.key_idea: Analyzed 140,000+ PLOS papers, defining thought leaders as authors responsible for conceptual tasks to measure their effect on team impact and disruptiveness.
card.evaluation: Correlational and causal analysis of 140,000+ papers from PLOS journals; examined interactions with team size, gender diversity, and international collaboration.

slides.title: NavIsaacLab: Generating Realistic Crowd via Parallel Robot Learning for Benchmarking Human-aware Navigation
slides.tldr: PHYSICS-BASED CROWD SIMULATION FOR HUMAN-AWARE NAVIGATION
slides.highlight: NavIsaacLab provides a framework for training and benchmarking human-aware navigation policies using photo-realistic, physics-based pedestrian simulations. This is relevant to RwB for improving safety and natural human-robot interaction in shared environments.

card.one_liner: NavIsaacLab is a GPU-parallelized simulation framework for benchmarking and training human-aware robot navigation policies.
card.key_idea: Combines a trajectory diffusion model with an adversarial motion learning (AMP) controller to generate physics-based, photorealistic, and controllable pedestrian behaviors within Isaac Lab.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 30 photorealistic scenes; compared against SFM and IsaacSim animations using success rates, pose entropy, and Motion-MMD metrics.
card.limitation: Some challenging locomotion transitions and long-tail motions remain difficult to reproduce accurately.

slides.title: BiPACE: Bisimulation-Guided Policy Optimization with Action Counterfactual Estimation for LLM Agents
slides.tldr: IMPROVED RL ADVANTAGE ESTIMATION FOR LLM AGENTS
slides.highlight: BiPACE introduces a bisimulation-guided policy optimization method to improve credit assignment for long-horizon LLM agents. This is relevant to MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: BiPACE improves LLM agent training by refining step-level credit assignment using behavioral clustering and action-conditioned baselines.
card.key_idea: BiGPO clusters actor hidden states via cosine distance to reduce singleton groups, while PACE uses action-conditioned peer baselines to nonparametrically estimate local Q-V advantages.
card.evaluation: Tested on ALFWorld, WebShop, and TextCraft using Qwen2.5 (1.5B/7B). BiPACE outperformed GRPO, GiGPO, and HGPO in success rates and sample efficiency.
card.limitation: Evaluated only on text-only environments with discrete action spaces; uses a fixed cosine radius epsilon determined by calibration.
